title: Route egregore Goal Gravity capability deficits into GREG Capability Genesis (C.G11)
problem: An egregore GoalGravityLoop goal whose active plan node requires a function the repertoire lacks records an egregore.capability_deficit and WAITs. Nothing read that record, so the goal stayed goal_blocked_not_closed for good, even when GREG's Capability Genesis could form the function from installed software. GREG's own Goal Gravity (greg/goal_gravity.py, _form_requested) already asks Genesis for GREG goals; the egregore runtime had no route.
founder_intent_refs: docs/FOUNDER_EFFECT_COMPILER.md: a new capability never inherits the authority of the process that requested or built it
baseline: #196 12119590: egregore deficits recorded and never consumed; GREG goal formation for GREG goals only.

alternatives.name: Proposed: an adapter that drafts an unsigned GREG mission and settles the egregore deficit from GREG's journal
alternatives.description: draft_missions reads open egregore deficits, skips halted goals and functions Genesis cannot form without a builder, and returns an unsigned read-only, zero-budget mission with no auto_attach whose signed provenance names the deficit; the caller supplies the check that senses the function. settle reads GREG's closure of the mission's deficit (deficit.resolved, or the founder's signed CAPABILITY_ATTACH of the capability Genesis verified for it), confirms the capability still serves ATTACHED, registers a read-only <function>@function genome and closes the egregore deficit with resolved_by linking the GREG record.
advantages: Reuses Genesis, its frozen oracle and the founder attach; builds only the missing seam
Holds no key and grants nothing: the founder signs the mission and attaches the capability
The egregore goal resumes through its own repertoire check (capability_present), unchanged
disadvantages: The founder must supply the check (the egregore goal carries no function inputs)
Two ledgers: the egregore runtime's and the Body's, linked by digests, not one
Couples to the capability.state 'by' string for founder attaches

alternatives.name: Host the egregore goal on the Body's own ledger
alternatives.description: Run GoalGravityLoop on body.ledger so one ledger holds both.
advantages: One ledger, as the gap text proposed
disadvantages: The Body's admission check pauses (stop_pushing) every egregore goal no founder-signed GOAL authorizes; such a goal is GREG's own and greg/goal_gravity.py already serves it
alternatives.revival_evidence: test_an_unsigned_egregore_goal_on_the_body_ledger_is_quarantined_and_never_drafted shows the quarantine; revive only if the founder wants unsigned egregore goals on a Body

alternatives.name: Let the adapter call Genesis.form_for_goal directly
alternatives.description: Skip the mission: form the function on the egregore goal's behalf under any open mission.
disadvantages: An unsigned egregore goal would spend a signed mission's scope; formation would run with no founder signature on the egregore side
alternatives.revival_evidence: a founder-signed egregore goal binding to a GREG mission

alternatives.name: Write deficit.resolved on founder attach in greg/body.py
alternatives.description: Fix GREG so a founder CAPABILITY_ATTACH resolves the mission's deficit, then settle on deficit.resolved only.
advantages: One closing record for both attach paths
disadvantages: Changes greg/body.py and greg/genesis.py outside this claim; touches several consumers (compounding, path, appraisal)
alternatives.revival_evidence: the Genesis owner takes the reported gap; settle then needs only the first branch

do_nothing_option.expected_outcome: An egregore goal blocked on a formable function stays blocked forever.
disadvantages: The two Goal Gravity runtimes stay disconnected from Genesis on one side

roles.position: A blocked goal should reach the capability it needs without the founder hand-relaying it, and without any authority moving.
material_concerns: The draft must never be signed by GREG

roles.position: Integration, not invention: two unchanged mechanisms (egregore deficits, GREG Genesis) joined by a typed adapter; no second genesis, ledger or router.
material_concerns: Do not choose the canonical Goal Gravity runtime (open founder decision)

roles.position: Attack settle with a detached, revoked or unformed capability and with halted goals; attack draft with unsigned inbox drops.
material_concerns: A stopped goal must not be resumed by a later settle

roles.position: Small module, idempotent records, no new process; the ablation shows what is lost without it.
material_concerns: Horizon is computed at drafting time; drafts made from an old clock expire

roles.position: Every closure names the GREG record it rests on; the original goal is never edited.
material_concerns: Two ledgers mean the link is a digest, not a shared record

evidence.claim: A blocked egregore goal resumes after Genesis forms the function and the founder attaches it
evidence.finding: next gravity turn classifies the move; without settle it still WAITs

halted status, serving capability, settle idempotence, draft once, formable and sensor match each caught; function match (founder-edited drafts only) and the founder-command 'by' check (backed by the command digest requirement) survive

counterevidence.claim: The adapter can run on the Body's ledger
counterevidence.finding: the Body's admission check paused the unsigned egregore goal; design changed to bridge two ledgers

counterevidence.claim: GREG writes deficit.resolved whenever a deficit closes
counterevidence.finding: a founder CAPABILITY_ATTACH writes none; settle links the signed attach instead and the gap is reported on #96

pass_1.intended_outcome: An egregore goal blocked on a function GREG can form resumes once the founder signs the drafted mission and attaches the result, with every step linked.

advantages.statement: A second Goal Gravity runtime now reaches Capability Genesis
advantages.amplified_value: Both runtimes gain the same formation path while the canonical one is undecided; settle feeds the egregore repertoire so later egregore goals needing the function are unblocked too

disadvantages.statement: The founder must supply the sensing check
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Unrouted functions are reported with a reason instead of guessed
The quarantine on the Body ledger is tested as the reason; resolved_by names the exact GREG record

disadvantages.statement: Founder-attach closures depend on the 'by' string
disadvantages.redesigned_response: Also require command_digest; report the missing deficit.resolved upstream

comparisons.strongest_competing_architecture: fix deficit.resolved in GREG and host the goal as a founder-signed GREG GOAL
comparisons.reversible_experiment: delete the module; records it wrote stay as history

rejected_alternatives.name: form_for_goal from the adapter
rejected_alternatives.rejection_reason: spends a signed mission's scope for an unsigned goal

pass_2.attack_summary: Attack the strengthened design: settle after the founder stops or revokes the goal, after a detach, twice on a partly formed deficit; drop the unsigned draft in the inbox; supply a check that does not sense the function.

new_weaknesses.statement: A stopped or revoked goal resumed by a later settle
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: settle and draft both refuse halted goals (tested)

new_weaknesses.statement: A check naming the function but sensing something else
new_weaknesses.strengthening_response: the sensor's function must equal the drafted function (tested)

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: the founder's check is the honest source of inputs
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: an egregore goal that carries function inputs

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: the Body ledger is GREG's; unsigned egregore goals are quarantined there by design
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: founder decides the canonical Goal Gravity runtime

pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.rationale: command digest required; upstream gap reported
pass_1_disadvantage_dispositions.review_trigger: GREG writes deficit.resolved on founder attach

pass_2.final_design: greg/gravity_genesis.py: draft_missions and settle, refusing halted goals, unformable functions and mismatched checks; settle requires the capability to still serve ATTACHED and links the closing GREG record.

residual_risks.risk: A new GREG attach path not recognized by settle
residual_risks.mitigation: the goal simply stays blocked; nothing is granted
residual_risks.review_trigger: a drafted mission ACHIEVED whose egregore deficit stays open

migration_plan: None; existing records are not rewritten.

steps: Or revert the commit; the records it wrote stay as history

kill_criteria: A drafted mission is applied without a founder signature
A halted goal is resumed by settle
review_trigger: Founder decision on the canonical Goal Gravity runtime, or GREG writing deficit.resolved on founder attach
